lens: Whether each reading actually supports the claim drawn from it or a weaker claim that resembles it; whether a passing test would also pass under a hypothesis the paper's conclusion excludes; and whether a row in the paper's own artifacts contradicts its prose.
what_i_read: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json (panels.ddr_mmej, panels.apoptotic_dependency, panels.p53_mdm2_axis, panels.chromatin_prc2_baf, panels.arginine_auxotrophy, panels.instrument_controls; gene_reads for POLQ/LIG3/PARP1/XRCC1/BRCA1/BRCA2/RAD51/RAD52/PALB2/ASS1/ASL/ARG1/ARG2/OTC/PMAIP1/MCL1/BCL2L1/BCL2/BCL2L2/BCL2A1/BCL2L11/BID/BAD/BIK/BAX/BAK1/EZH2/EED/SUZ12/RBBP4/SMARCB1/SMARCA4/ARID1A/PBRM1/MDM2/TP53/CDKN1A/NR4A3/ENO3/MKI67/PCNA/MCM2/TOP2A)
research/modalities/census-route-expression-grading.json (all 16 route rows, RT-POLQ and RT-APOPTOSIS-DEP in full)
research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-null-background.json (existence and scope of the random-gene-set null)
research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-confounds.json (precedent for a withdrawn cross-platform module claim; comparator-arm exclusion accounting)
central_claim: For five therapeutic classes selected on a molecular state rather than a histology, public EMC expression data (16 archival tumours, two array series) shows the selecting state is absent in four; the paper's stated methodological contribution is that the four negatives differ in strength and that grading each one honestly is the whole job.

blockers.summary: Section 2.4's specificity claim is refuted by the paper's own artifact on one of its two platforms. The paper writes that the NHEJ contrast being flat means 'the elevation is specific rather than a general repair-transcription effect'. On GSE4303/GPL3290 the homologous-recombination module rose MORE than the alt-EJ module (+0.2658 vs +0.2578 SD units), and the proliferation reference MKI67 rose +1.2358 SD on that same platform. A proliferation- or cellularity-driven rise produces exactly the observed pattern — alt-EJ up, HR up, NHEJ flat — because c-NHEJ is the one double-strand-break arm that is not S/G2-restricted, so the single control the paper chose is structurally unable to detect the alternative it claims to have excluded. The paper's own falsifier F8 names this hypothesis and lists it as untested; the observation that fires it is already committed in the artifact the paper cites.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json, panels.ddr_mmej.groups on GSE4303-GPL3290: alt_ej_module score.delta_a_minus_b = 0.2578 (t=2.226); homologous_recombination score.delta_a_minus_b = 0.2658 (t=1.035); nhej_contrast delta = 0.0218 (t=0.158). Same file, gene_reads.MKI67 GSE4303-GPL3290 verdict = 'HIGHER in EMC by 1.2358 SD units of the array (|t| 2-3, t=2.301, df=5.5, n_EMC=9, n_comparator=6)'. Same file, panels.instrument_controls.expected.MKI67 = 'approximately FLAT in GSE24369. EMC is slow-cycling; a large proliferation delta would say the contrast is being driven by cellularity.' The artifact sets that expectation only for GSE24369 and the manuscript never reports MKI67 on either platform. Cross-check: census-route-expression-grading.json, routes.RT-TXN-CDK.what_this_does_not_settle already records for these same two series that 'A general-transcription elevation is also exactly what higher cellularity or proliferation would produce.'
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Report MKI67 on both platforms; withdraw or restrict 'specific rather than a general repair-transcription effect' to GPL6244, where MKI67 is flat (t=0.528) and the alt-EJ/HR separation is +0.087 vs -0.044; and state that on GPL3290 the alt-EJ and HR modules move together by the same amount, so that platform contributes no evidence of specificity. Adding a proliferation-matched or S/G2-gene contrast arm to the panel would settle it; quoting t-statistics instead of effect sizes is what currently hides it, since t = 2.23 for alt-EJ against t = 1.04 for HR is a variance difference and not an effect-size difference.

blockers.summary: The sole observation that keeps the sole surviving class open is a one-platform reading presented as a two-platform one, and the group it belongs to moves the opposite way on the platform in question. Section 2.5 states 'NOXA ... is HIGHER in EMC on both platforms'. On GPL6244 that reading is t = 0.628, which the source artifact itself labels '|t| < 2 — flat' — the same band the manuscript calls flat three paragraphs earlier for the NHEJ contrast (t = -0.19 and 0.16) and for the p53 axis genes. On that platform the BH3-only sensitiser GROUP is LOWER in EMC (t = -0.168) and the only two sensitisers with |t| > 2 both go DOWN (BCL2L11 t = -2.575; BIK t = -2.105), while the effectors are also down (group t = -2.105; BAX individually t = -4.045). The parsimonious reading of GPL6244 is that the whole BCL-2 family reads lower together — guardians, effectors and sensitisers — which is a global or dilution effect, not the 'low guardians with a high sensitiser' priming picture the paper infers. The priming inference holds on GPL3290 alone and is stated without that qualifier.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json, gene_reads.PMAIP1 GSE24369 verdict = 'HIGHER in EMC by 0.2292 SD units of the array (|t| < 2 — flat, t=0.628, df=5.9, n_EMC=6, n_comparator=29)'; GSE4303-GPL3290 verdict = 'HIGHER in EMC by 1.7441 SD units ... (|t| >= 3, t=7.594, df=12.8, n_EMC=10, n_comparator=5)'. panels.apoptotic_dependency.groups.bh3_only_sensitisers GSE24369 verdict = 'LOWER in EMC by 0.0134 SD units (t=-0.168, df=6.3 ...)'; groups.effectors GSE24369 = 'LOWER in EMC by 0.0677 SD units (t=-2.105 ...)'. gene_reads.BCL2L11 GSE24369 t=-2.575; gene_reads.BIK GSE24369 t=-2.105; gene_reads.BAX GSE24369 'LOWER in EMC by 0.1254 SD units of the array (|t| >= 3, t=-4.045 ...)'. Manuscript §2.4 uses the flat convention explicitly ('the non-homologous end-joining contrast is flat on both (t = -0.19 and 0.16)') and §2.2 grades t = -1.13 as weak, so the convention exists and is not applied here.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: State that the NOXA elevation is significant on GPL3290 (t = 7.59) and flat on GPL6244 (t = 0.63) by the paper's own convention, and that the sensitiser group as a whole is flat-to-lower on GPL6244 while two of its five members are significantly lower there. Then either restrict the priming sentence to GPL3290 or restate it as a single-platform observation. The class can still be reported as the one that stays open — that conclusion rests on the instrument's inability to measure dependency and survives — but the affirmative 'transcriptional shadow of a primed cell' claim does not survive as a two-platform statement.

p1s.summary: Section 2.4 never reports POLQ — the polymerase the class is named for, the panel's declared primary_gene, and the only alt-EJ-specific member of the module. On the one platform where it is readable it is flat (t = 0.309) and sits at the 21st percentile of that array; on the other it is not readable at all. The module's cross-platform 'concordance' is therefore carried entirely by PARP1, XRCC1 and LIG3 — the canonical single-strand-break-repair/BER machinery, not Pol-theta-mediated end joining. The paper's own cited grading artifact carries this caveat verbatim and the manuscript drops it.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json, gene_reads.POLQ GSE24369 = 'READABLE on GPL6244 (1 probe(s)); EMC samples sit at the 21th percentile of this array's probe distribution. HIGHER in EMC by 0.0446 SD units of the array (|t| < 2 — flat, t=0.309, df=7.6, n_EMC=6, n_comparator=29)'; GSE4303-GPL3290 = 'NOT READABLE on GPL3290 — the read could not be taken', n_probes_mapping = 0. panels.ddr_mmej.primary_gene = 'POLQ'; groups.alt_ej_module genes_requested = [POLQ, LIG3, PARP1, XRCC1], on GPL3290 genes_not_readable = [POLQ]. research/modalities/census-route-expression-grading.json, routes.RT-POLQ.observed ends: 'The route's own primary gene is a weaker reading than its module: it is readable on only ONE platform, is barely higher there, and sits in the bottom quarter of that array's distribution — so the module carries this observation and the single gene does not.' No sentence in the manuscript conveys this.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Report POLQ's own reading in 2.4 and restate the module claim as 'three alt-EJ-associated genes, none of them the polymerase this class targets, are higher on both platforms'. The current sentence 'every readable member is higher on both' is literally true and is exactly what makes the omission invisible; and PARP1/XRCC1/LIG3 are a single-strand-break-repair complex, so an SSBR/BER contrast arm — not the NHEJ arm — is the control this module needs.

p1s.summary: The paper's threshold for calling a reading real moves in the direction of its conclusions. It grades on the t-statistic, which at df 5-15 in a Welch test is dominated by variance rather than effect size, and every instance of the drift favours the paper's reading.
p1s.evidence: From research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json group scores, matched against the manuscript's own words: alt_ej_module on GPL6244, delta = +0.087 SD, t = 2.423 -> manuscript: 'The alt-EJ half IS present, concordantly'. prc2_core on GPL3290, delta = +0.2509 SD, t = 1.714 -> manuscript: 'the rest of PRC2 is flat'. gene_reads.EZH2 on GPL3290, delta = +0.6291 SD, t = 2.839 -> manuscript: 'EZH2 is mildly higher on both platforms'. homologous_recombination on GPL3290, delta = +0.2658 SD, t = 1.035 -> manuscript: 'flat to mildly *higher*'. The single reading the paper calls present has the SMALLEST effect size of any group it grades, and the largest single-gene effect in the five classes (EZH2, +0.63 SD) is the one it dismisses as mild.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Quote delta_a_minus_b beside every t, or move to a stated effect-size threshold applied identically to all five classes. Note also that census-route-expression-grading.json's own header rule says 'Magnitudes are NOT comparable across the two platforms; only sign agreement is', which the manuscript's paired t-quotes ('t = 2.42 and 2.23') read against.

p1s.summary: The n reported in Section 1's table is not the n behind the numbers on GSE4303. The table states 10 EMC vs 6 comparator as a fixed design; 117 of the 418 readable gene-reads on that platform run at less than 10 v 6, including one the manuscript quotes.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json gene_reads, GSE4303-GPL3290 entries: counted 418 readable gene-reads, 301 at n_EMC=10/n_comparator=6, 117 at reduced n (as low as n_EMC=2, n_comparator=1). Specific rows the manuscript relies on: gene_reads.PMAIP1 GPL3290 n_EMC=10, n_comparator=5 (this is the 1.74 SD figure quoted in §2.5); gene_reads.RAD51 GPL3290 n_EMC=8, df=2.2; gene_reads.PALB2 GPL3290 df=4.2; gene_reads.BCL2L11 GPL3290 n_EMC=9, n_comparator=3; gene_reads.ARID1A GPL3290 n_EMC=9. Most striking: gene_reads.NR4A3 GPL3290 = 'No group contrast — n_EMC=9, n_comparator=2; the floor is 3 per group. No contrast computed' — the disease-defining gene cannot be contrasted at all on the platform carrying 10 of the paper's 16 tumours.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Add a footnote to the §1 table stating that per-gene n on GPL3290 varies with probe-level missingness, give the range, and carry the actual n alongside every GPL3290 figure quoted in the text.

p1s.summary: The manuscript reports no positive control. The source artifact states its own precondition — 'A panel of six reads is worth nothing until the instrument has produced a known answer' and 'A read that does not recover this [NR4A3 UP] is an instrument failure, not a biological finding' — and the pipeline does recover it at gene level, favourably, on GPL6244. The paper says none of this, and also omits the one place the control fails.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json, panels.instrument_controls.question = 'Does this pipeline reproduce readings whose answer is already known, on these exact platforms? A panel of six reads is worth nothing until the instrument has produced a known answer.' gene_reads.NR4A3 GSE24369 = 'HIGHER in EMC by 0.7415 SD units of the array (|t| >= 3, t=4.662, df=7.2)'; gene_reads.ENO3 GSE24369 t=3.607 and GSE4303-GPL3290 t=13.221 at the 98th percentile. But panels.instrument_controls.groups.fusion_and_its_published_direct_target emits NO SCORE on either platform ('UNDERPOWERED — 2/2 genes readable ... the floor for a curated panel is 3 genes'), groups.proliferation_reference (MKI67) likewise emits NO SCORE, and gene_reads.NR4A3 on GPL3290 has no contrast computable. The manuscript contains no sentence about NR4A3, ENO3 or MKI67 as controls.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Add a short instrument-validation paragraph to §1 reporting NR4A3 and ENO3 recovery per platform, and stating that on GPL3290 the NR4A3 contrast is not computable while ENO3 is strongly recovered. This is favourable to the paper and its absence is a gift to a hostile referee.

p1s.summary: 'Low guardians' is a relative-to-comparator statement, and §2.5 converts it into an absolute-abundance premise to reach a priming conclusion. In absolute terms on GPL6244 the guardians are among the most highly expressed genes on the array and the sensitiser is not.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json array percentiles on GSE24369/GPL6244: MCL1 97th, BCL2L1 82nd, BCL2 61st, BCL2L2 68th, PMAIP1 (NOXA) 60th. The paper's priming inference is a stoichiometric claim about which protein holds the effectors, but on GPL6244 the guardians sit above the sensitiser in absolute array terms — the reverse of the priming picture — and the whole claim rests on the between-group contrast alone. The artifact's own panels.apoptotic_dependency.what_it_cannot_settle says 'APOPTOTIC DEPENDENCY IS NOT AN ABUNDANCE'. The manuscript's §5 acknowledges relativity generally but §2.5 makes the absolute inference without flagging it.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State the array percentiles beside the contrast in §2.5, and mark the priming sentence explicitly as a statement about EMC relative to comparator sarcomas rather than about absolute guardian abundance.

p2s.summary: ASS1's absolute percentile is quoted only on the platform where it is impressive. §2.1 gives '92nd percentile' on GPL6244 and omits that on GPL3290 ASS1 sits at the 41st percentile — middling, despite the +1.55 SD contrast.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/census-route-expression-grading.json, routes.RT-ARGININE.genes.ASS1: GSE24369 emc_array_percentile 0.9152; GSE4303-GPL3290 emc_array_percentile 0.4053, delta_emc_minus_comparator 1.5503. The grading artifact records both; the manuscript quotes one. This does not weaken the negative (41st percentile is not 'low' either) but the asymmetry is the mirror image of the P1 above and a referee will notice both.

p2s.summary: A random-gene-set null background exists on both platforms and is applied to none of the five classes, despite a standing instruction in the paper's own cited grading artifact — added after a cross-platform curated-module elevation was WITHDRAWN on exactly that test. The alt-EJ elevation is the same shape as the withdrawn claim.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-null-background.json: 3,978 random mapped background symbols on GSE24369 (of 18,724 on-platform), seeded, per platform, '_why_two_want_sets' explains it exists so a random-gene-set null can be drawn from the transcriptome. research/modalities/census-route-expression-grading.json header '_a_grader_must_read_the_audit_not_only_the_reading' = 'ADDED AFTER THIS FILE GOT IT WRONG ... Grading from the first without the second produced a SUPPORTED verdict on a signature its own genome-wide null restricts to one of the two platforms ... Any future grader over this panel must check whether a confound audit exists for the read it is using.' routes.RT-HYPOXIA-PRODRUG is now 'WITHDRAWN'. The manuscript is a grader over this panel and reports no null test for any of its five classes.

p2s.summary: §2.3's claim is about individual subunits but the statistics quoted are group statistics. 'No SWI/SNF tumour-suppressor subunit reads anywhere near a floor (t = -1.02 and -0.08)' cites the swi_snf_tumour_suppressors group score, which cannot establish a per-subunit statement. The per-gene data does support the claim, so this is a citation-of-the-wrong-statistic issue rather than a wrong claim.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json, panels.chromatin_prc2_baf.groups.swi_snf_tumour_suppressors: GSE24369 t=-1.024, GSE4303-GPL3290 t=-0.083 — these are the two numbers in the manuscript sentence. Per-gene array percentiles that actually support it: SMARCB1 77th/52nd, SMARCA4 82nd/53rd, ARID1A 83rd/18th, PBRM1 55th/36th. ARID1A at the 18th percentile on GPL3290 is the closest any subunit comes to a floor and is not mentioned; SMARCB1 individually is t=-2.164 on GPL6244, masked by the group score.

p2s.summary: Terminology collision on 'selectivity' between the manuscript and the dependency artifact it cites. §2.5 says the near-universal MCL1/BCL2L1 dependency 'argues against selectivity'; the artifact's own selectivity field says MCL1 IS sarcoma-selective.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json, _note defines 'selectivity = rest_mean - sarcoma_mean (>0 = sarcoma-selective)'. genes_by_group['Apoptotic guardians (BH3)']: MCL1 selectivity 0.139, sarcoma_frac_dependent 0.835 vs rest_frac_dependent 0.696; BCL2L1 selectivity -0.2, sarcoma_frac_dependent 0.758 vs rest 0.854. The manuscript's sense is therapeutic-window-vs-normal-tissue; the artifact's sense is sarcoma-vs-other-cancer. A reader with both open sees a contradiction that is only lexical. Also: the artifact's top-level n_sarcoma_models is 176 while every gene row carries n_sarcoma = 91, and the manuscript quotes no n for the dependency axis.

_verdict_note: supported_with_reservations rather than not_supported_as_written, because I attacked the four class exclusions directly and they held: ASS1 is concordantly higher on both platforms with large t (4.429 and 4.513) and the whole urea-cycle context is up alongside it (urea_cycle_context t=3.673 on GPL6244) — corroboration the paper does not even claim; the p53 axis genes really are flat (t=-0.601, 0.432) with the output group lower on both, and the paper grades that weak and says outright it cannot establish TP53 status; no SWI/SNF subunit is anywhere near a floor on the per-gene percentiles; the HR arm really is not down; and 'no EMC line in the dependency panel' is confirmed by the artifact's own _note. I also went looking for a sample-selection problem in GSE24369 (42 GSMs against 6+29=35 used) and found the exclusions properly accounted — seven 'unclassified' samples, five solitary fibrous tumours and two pooled skeletal-muscle RNA controls, removed from BOTH arms (emc-hypoxia-confounds.json, platforms.GSE24369 C1_C2 block). So the paper's negatives survive a hostile read. Not accept-with-minor-revision, because both blockers attach to the paper's two AFFIRMATIVE observations — the alt-EJ 'specificity' claim and the NOXA priming claim — and those are the sentences a reader would act on, being the only two places the paper tells anyone to spend money. The unifying defect is that the manuscript's stated methodological contribution is grading the strength of each reading honestly, and it applies that convention strictly to the four negatives (weak, weak, weakest) and not at all to the two positives: a t=0.628 reading is reported as directional while a t=-1.13 reading three sections earlier is graded weak, and a +0.087 SD module is 'present, concordantly' while a +0.63 SD gene is 'mildly higher'. Every fix is prose plus two numbers already sitting in the artifacts (MKI67, POLQ) — no new data is required, which is why this is major revision and not rejection.
